content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4 (split overtime, delayed breaks, coaching cancelled) for 14:00-16:00, but it only lifts service level to 40.6% against an 80% target, so bring in the duty manager now.","why":"The drop is caused by slow systems, not extra calls. Payments handle time rose to 561 s against a forecast of about 295 s. This matches P2 incident INC-20261102-2029 (core banking screens freezing, account-summary API over 8 s p95). Volume and absences are normal. No plan reaches 80%. P4 gives the best predicted service level for 14:00-16:00 at 40.6%, compared with 38.7% for doing nothing. It also cuts abandons from 20.7% to 19.3% and costs INR 1,560. It is the only plan that clearly helps both queues: payments goes to 44.4% and general to 35.4%. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 75.4%.","trade_offs":["P1 costs nothing, but at 38.8% it is barely better than doing nothing.","P3 and R1 cost more (INR 2,088) and give slightly lower abandons (18.6%) and payments service level (45.1%). However, their overall service level is lower (40.2%), and general falls to 33.5%.","Putting all 4 overtime agents on payments (P3) helps payments at the expense of general. P4 splits the overtime, which protects general.","P4 does not use callback or chat deflection. Those levers add cost but gave little extra benefit in the predictions."],"watch":"Escalation is required. The best compliant plan is predicted at about 41% for 14:00-16:00, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager should be involved, because the only real fix is resolving the system incident. Track progress on INC-20261102-2029 and payments handle time. Also watch general queue service level and abandons after overtime starts at 14:30."}
